description: Heracles, son of Zeus, kills his family in a fit of madness. His Twelve Labors are a penance: slaying monsters, then defeating death itself.

hero.hook: Twelve tests to clear a crime. A demigod who ends up among the gods.

blocks.text: **Heracles**, called **Hercules** by the Romans, is the greatest Greek hero. Son of , king of the gods, and the mortal **Alcmène**, he is not only a colossus. He embodies strength, but also violence and redemption. [[Zeus]]

His **Twelve Works** are not a voluntary quest for glory. It is a penance for a terrible crime. By purging the world of monsters, Heracles opens the way to civilization... and gains, a rare privilege, immortality.

, legitimate wife of Zeus, hates the child born from infidelity. From the cradle, she sends two snakes. The infant suffocates them with his bare hands. Later, [[Hera]]cles married **Mégara**, daughter of the king of Thebes. Hera then drives him mad: he massacres his wife and children.

This blood crime, a [[Miasma]], places him outside of society. The oracle of Delphi orders him to serve his cousin, king **Eurystheus**. This fearful sovereign, guided by Hera, imposes ten labors on him, then twelve, because he refuses to count some of them.
According to legend, Hera's milk, spouted from her breast while she was trickingly breastfeeding Heracles, would have formed the **Milky Way** in the sky.

The first challenge is the **Nemean Lion**, with impenetrable skin. Heracles strangles him, then skins him with his own claws. This skin, the [[Leonte]], becomes his armor. Next comes the **Lern Hydra**, a snake with many heads: for each head cut off, two grow back. With his nephew Iolaos, he cauterizes the necks with fire.

blocks.caption: Heracles facing the Nemean Lion and the Hydra.

blocks.text: The Ancients said that Zeus had placed the Nemean Lion among the stars: the constellation **Lion**.

The **Augean Stables** change register. Thousands of oxen have not been cleaned for thirty years. Eurystheus wants to humiliate the hero. Heracles diverts the rivers  and Peneus: in one day, the current carries away the manure. Intelligence is as good as brawn. [[Alphée]]

The work takes him away from Greece: Bull of Crete, man-eating mares, belt of **Hippolyte**, queen of the Amazons. For the herd of the giant **Géryon**, in the far West, Heracles opened a passage between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic: the [[The Pillars of Hercules]], today the Strait of Gibraltar.

He steals the **golden apples** from the Hesperides by tricking the titan , who carries the sky. The last job is the most terrible: going down to the Underworld and bringing back **Cerberus**, the many-headed dog. Coming out alive is symbolically defeating death. [[Atlas]]
The explorer Orellana would have named the river **Amazon** after believing he saw warrior women on its banks, echoing the Amazons of the myth.

sections.title: To the ends of the world

blocks.text: The Works end, but not the tragedies. His wife **Déjanire** makes him wear a tunic soaked in the poisonous blood of  Nessus. Burned alive, Heracles climbs onto a pyre on Mount Oeta. His mortal part burns. Its divine essence rises towards Olympus: it is the **apotheosis**. [[Centaur]]

blocks.caption: The apotheosis of Heracles: the hero joins the gods.

blocks.text: Reconciled with Hera, he marries **Hebé**, eternal youth. The Romans adopted his figure under the name **Hercules**. “Herculean work” still means an immense task. Heracles is not just a slayer of monsters: he is an architect of order.
**Heracles** (Hercules) performs twelve labors to atone for the murder of his family. From the Nemean Lion to Cerberus, he goes from chaos to civilization... and gains immortality.
